REQ mixes calendar years, Australian financial years, quarters and months.
The observation contract keeps the normalized period alongside
`period_start`, `period_end`, `period_basis` and `frequency`. Status, unit,
currency, price basis and geography are semantic dimensions, not display
decorations.

## Period statuses and missing values

Status suffixes are explicit when the source publishes them. A date alone is
not used to guess a status.

```{r status}
library(readreq)

req_status(c("2025-26s", "2026-27f", "2029-30z", "2024-25"))
```

Missing markers remain distinct from numeric zero. The returned reason is
controlled vocabulary; the original token is retained by parsed observations
in `raw_value`.

```{r missingness}
markers <- c(NA, "", "na", "n/a", "not available", "c", "..", "12")
data.frame(
  raw_value = markers,
  missing_reason = req_missing_reason(markers),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

The synthetic workbook makes the same contract visible on real parser output.

```{r fixture-contract}
forecast_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "readreq-example-forecast.xlsx", package = "readreq"
)
if (!nzchar(forecast_path)) {
  forecast_path <- file.path(
    "..", "inst", "extdata", "readreq-example-forecast.xlsx"
  )
}
stopifnot(nzchar(forecast_path), file.exists(forecast_path))

period_cache <- tempfile("readreq-period-cache-")
dir.create(period_cache, recursive = TRUE)
forecast <- read_req_forecasts(
  forecast_path,
  view = "reported",
  cache_dir = period_cache
)

head(
  forecast[
    !is.na(forecast$missing_reason),
    c("period", "period_status", "unit", "value", "raw_value", "missing_reason")
  ]
)
```

## Troubleshooting by condition class

Failures are typed so that callers can distinguish discovery, transport,
format, workbook-schema, cell-parse, unit, stitching and general validation
problems. Start with the condition class and message, then record the exact
release ID, asset, sheet or table, cache directory and a small reproducible
input.

```{r typed-error}
failure <- tryCatch(
  req_missing_reason("unexpected marker"),
  error = function(e) list(
    class = class(e),
    message = conditionMessage(e)
  )
)
failure
```

Useful responses include:

- `req_release_discovery_error` or `req_download_error`: check HTTPS access,
  the exact release ID and whether an exact cache can be replayed offline.
- `req_asset_format_error`: verify that the downloaded bytes are the expected
  XLS/XLSX/PDF asset, not an HTML error page.
- `req_workbook_schema_error`, `req_sheet_parse_error`, or
  `req_period_parse_error`: preserve the original workbook and report the
  release, sheet and table; do not rename sheets or drop unexplained cells.
- `req_unit_conflict_error` or `req_stitch_conflict_error`: use
  `view = "reported"` to inspect source presentations before relying on a
  canonical or current view.
- `req_validation_error`: inspect the returned context and repair the input or
  source selection rather than suppressing the failure.

Only the two audited report-only editions use the PDF table fallback. If that
path is selected, install Poppler so that `pdftotext` is available; Poppler is
not required for ordinary workbook reads. Official report PDFs and workbook
values are not fixtures. Their rights and exclusions remain edition-specific,
and `req_attribution()` provides package-level attribution guidance.
